question: Is Gunsight Mountain's West Ridge (class 3 scramble) a real climbed route, to be added on or_gunsight_mountain?
answer: Yes. The Oregon Hikers field guide names a straightforward scramble up the west ridge from Lower Hoffer Lake. An Oct 2024 Oregon Hikers trip report climbed it from Hoffer Lakes: easy 2nd class rising to optional 3rd class boulders and slabs. A SummitPost route page exists (Hoffer Lakes West Ridge) but returned 403; its snippet says steep class 3. Reports pair it with a class 2 South Ridge descent. The approach is the shoreline trail from the Anthony Lake day-use lot, then the signed Hoffer Lakes trail (about 0.7 mi), then an unofficial path east to the rock outcrop at the base of the ridge. The lake area is marshy in summer.
recommendation: Add route West Ridge on or_gunsight_mountain: discipline scrambling, grade Class 2-3, face W, season Jul-Oct (logged ascents also in May and Dec on snow, so say Jul-Oct for the dry scramble). Overview, approach and descent in our own words below. No trailhead pin (no coordinate fetched).

proposed.name: West Ridge
proposed.overview: A ridge scramble that begins as easy walking and steepens into optional third-class boulders and slabs, with the line adjustable between easy slopes and harder rock. Wet ground around the lakes in summer is common.
proposed.approach: From the Anthony Lake day-use area, take the lakeshore path to the signed Hoffer Lakes trail and follow it to the lakes. An informal path leads east to a rock outcrop on the far shore, where the ridge begins.
proposed.descent_text: Walk down the gentler South Ridge (class 2), or drop the southeast side on game trails into Angell Basin and return past the Hoffer Lakes.
